# v2.89-dev

Security hardening release, continuing the review that produced v2.88-dev. This
one is about boundaries: where the server is allowed to write files, and how
much a failed connection test is allowed to tell you. Two settings are new and
optional, and one of them needs a look if your scheduled exports write outside
the application directory — see **Upgrading**.

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes below say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

## Hardened

- **Scheduled exports saved to the server now write inside one folder.** A
  **Local Filesystem** export delivers into the server's exports folder —
  `exports` in the application directory unless the new `EXPORT_ROOT` setting
  says otherwise. Type a name such as `monthly` in **Output Path** for a
  sub-folder, or leave it blank for the folder itself; it is created for you on
  the first run. Anywhere else is refused when you save the schedule, and also
  when it runs, so a schedule created before this release cannot quietly keep
  using an old location.

- **The "keep last N" setting can no longer delete more than it should.** A
  non-whole number entered there used to be treated as zero *after* the
  housekeeping had already started, which cleared the folder instead of trimming
  it. The value is now rounded down and applied consistently, and the tidy-up
  only ever considers files, never anything else in the folder.

- **The backup folder picker stays inside the backups folder.** **Browse** now
  opens at `backups` in the application directory — or wherever the new
  `BACKUP_ROOT` setting points — and cannot be navigated above it. This matches
  the rule **Save** has always applied, so no folder you could actually have
  used has been taken away. The same folder is now the single source of truth
  for where backups are written and read, rather than being worked out
  separately in four places.

- **Connection tests say less about the network.** **Test Connection** and the
  credential health checks now report a short fixed reason — the credentials
  were rejected, the host and port could not be reached, or the server name
  could not be resolved — instead of repeating the underlying network error. The
  full detail goes to the server log, which is where it is actually useful. The
  same applies to the error recorded against a schedule when a delivery fails.

- **A connection test to an unresponsive host now gives up in seconds** rather
  than after roughly two minutes, so checking all your providers no longer ties
  up the server while one of them hangs.

## Upgrading

No database changes; the update applies automatically.

Two things are worth checking afterwards:

- **If a scheduled export writes to a folder outside the application
  directory** — a mounted share, for instance — set `EXPORT_ROOT` in `.env` to
  the folder that contains it and restart the service. Until you do, that
  schedule reports an error instead of running, and the error names this
  setting. Exports using the default location need no action.
- **On a systemd host, a folder outside `/opt/training-tracker`** also needs a
  matching `ReadWritePaths=` line added via a drop-in, followed by
  `systemctl daemon-reload`; the service is sandboxed and will otherwise be
  refused permission to write there. The same applies to `BACKUP_ROOT`.

Both settings are documented in `.env.example`, the README and the in-app help
(**Scheduled Report Exports** and **Backup & Restore**).
